protocol.description:
Whether a window covers the rectangle the dock shows itself in, for the dock's intellihide. The client names its layer surface and the rectangle it occupies when it is not hidden; the compositor says whether a window covers that rectangle, and when that changes, and nothing else about windows. The compositor offers the manager only to the clients it trusts with it; it is Athanor's own protocol (doc_own_stack.md decision 35).
A new version adds interfaces, requests, events or enum entries; a client binds the version it knows.

interface.name: athanor_dock_overlap_manager_v1
interface.description: Makes the overlap object of a layer surface.

entry.name: not_layer_surface
entry.summary: the surface has no zwlr_layer_surface_v1 role

request.name: destroy
request.description: The overlap objects made from the manager stay valid.

request.name: get_overlap

description.summary: the overlap of a layer surface

request.description: Makes the overlap object of a surface that has the zwlr_layer_surface_v1 role; any other surface is the not_layer_surface error. The object sends nothing until its first set_rectangle.

interface.name: athanor_dock_overlap_v1

description.summary: whether windows cover the dock's rectangle

interface.description: The answer for the rectangle last set: whether a mapped window, not minimised, of the current workspace of the layer surface's output intersects it. The answer depends on that rectangle only, not on where the surface is drawn, so that hiding the surface does not change it.

event.name: overlapped

description.summary: whether a window covers the rectangle

event.description: 1 when such a window intersects the rectangle, 0 when none does. Sent after the first set_rectangle and then at each change of the answer. While the session is locked nothing is sent; at unlock the current answer is sent, changed or not.

request.name: set_rectangle

description.summary: the rectangle the dock occupies when shown

request.description: The rectangle the surface occupies when it is not hidden, in the logical coordinates of its output, its origin at the output's top left corner. The client sends it again when its size, its position or the output's scale changes. A rectangle without area intersects nothing.
